description: Average copies per film (per rating and overall) are computed only over films that have at least one copy in inventory. Films with no copies are excluded.

a.request: Looking only at films that have at least one copy in inventory (films with no copies are left out completely, including from every average), count each film's inventory copies. For each film, show its id, its rating, its number of copies, its copy count minus the average copy count per film for films of the same rating, and its copy count minus the overall average copy count per film (averaged over the individual films, not over the rating averages; averages ignore missing values). Sort by the difference from the overall average, largest first, and keep the top 10 (ties broken arbitrarily). Do not round.
a.sql: WITH fc AS (SELECT f.film_id, f.rating, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copies FROM film f JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.film_id, f.rating), stats AS (SELECT film_id, rating, copies, AVG(copies) OVER (PARTITION BY rating) AS rating_avg, AVG(copies) OVER () AS overall_avg FROM fc) SELECT film_id, rating, copies, copies - rating_avg AS diff_from_rating_avg, copies - overall_avg AS diff_from_overall_avg FROM stats ORDER BY diff_from_overall_avg DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: Which 10 films have the most inventory copies compared with the average number of copies per film? For each, show the film id, its rating, its number of copies, how far that is from the average copies per film for its rating, and how far it is from the overall average copies per film (averaged over films, not over the rating averages; averages ignore missing values). Sort by the overall difference, largest first. Ties can go in any order, and nothing is rounded. Average copies per film (per rating and overall) are computed only over films that have at least one copy in inventory. Films with no copies are excluded.
c.sql: WITH film_copies AS (SELECT f.film_id, f.rating, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copies FROM film f JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.film_id, f.rating), rating_avg AS (SELECT rating, AVG(copies) AS rating_avg_copies FROM film_copies GROUP BY rating), overall AS (SELECT AVG(copies) AS overall_avg_copies FROM film_copies) SELECT fc.film_id, fc.rating, fc.copies, fc.copies - ra.rating_avg_copies AS diff_from_rating_avg, fc.copies - o.overall_avg_copies AS diff_from_overall_avg FROM film_copies fc JOIN rating_avg ra ON ra.rating <=> fc.rating CROSS JOIN overall o ORDER BY diff_from_overall_avg DESC LIMIT 10;

b.request: Among films with at least one inventory copy, list the top 10 by (copy count − overall average copies per film), where the overall average is taken over only those films and each film's copy count is compared with the average copy count of films sharing its rating (also computed over only films with ≥1 copy), returning film_id, rating, copy count, difference from its rating average, and difference from the overall average, sorted by the overall difference descending with no rounding
b.sql: WITH film_copies AS (SELECT f.film_id, f.rating, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copy_count FROM film f JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.film_id, f.rating), rating_avg AS (SELECT rating, AVG(copy_count) AS rating_avg_copies FROM film_copies GROUP BY rating), overall AS (SELECT AVG(copy_count) AS overall_avg_copies FROM film_copies) SELECT fc.film_id, fc.rating, fc.copy_count, fc.copy_count - ra.rating_avg_copies AS diff_from_rating_avg, fc.copy_count - o.overall_avg_copies AS diff_from_overall_avg FROM film_copies fc JOIN rating_avg ra ON ra.rating = fc.rating CROSS JOIN overall o ORDER BY diff_from_overall_avg DESC LIMIT 10;

d.request: Which films with at least one copy in inventory have the most inventory copies relative to the average copies per film? For each, show the film id, its rating, its number of copies, how far that is from the average copies per film for its rating, and how far it is from the overall average copies per film (averaged over films with at least one copy, not over the rating averages; averages ignore missing values). Sort by the overall difference, largest first. Ties can go in any order, and nothing is rounded.
d.sql: WITH film_copies AS (SELECT f.film_id, f.rating, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copies FROM film f JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.film_id, f.rating), overall AS (SELECT AVG(copies) AS overall_avg FROM film_copies), rating_avg AS (SELECT rating, AVG(copies) AS rating_avg FROM film_copies GROUP BY rating) SELECT fc.film_id, fc.rating, fc.copies, fc.copies - ra.rating_avg AS diff_from_rating_avg, fc.copies - o.overall_avg AS diff_from_overall_avg FROM film_copies fc JOIN rating_avg ra ON ra.rating = fc.rating CROSS JOIN overall o ORDER BY diff_from_overall_avg DESC
